# Design

Read these rules before you add or change a helper, a public entry, a name, or a setup error. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="fr-06"></a>

## FR-06: Symmetry wherever it costs nothing `[HOLD]`

> Two things that do the same job take the same shape, order, and names.

Old number: 2.2.

Check: impossible.

The three decryption paths, the two user paths, the
`Args` structs, the `OnForkStack` / `OnCleartextStack` pairs: if two things do the same job they take
the same shape, in the same order, with the same names. A reader who learns one has learned the
other. Break symmetry only for a measured reason — a stack-too-deep, a gas cost — and write that
reason where the asymmetry is.

<a id="fr-09"></a>

## FR-09: A cheat must be unmistakable `[HOLD]`

> The names and the docs of a cheat show that it proves nothing about access.

Old number: 2.5.

Check: impossible.

`StdFhevmCheatsSafe.plaintextOf` bypasses permits, the ACL
and the KMS. It proves nothing about access; `decrypt` is what tests that. Keep that distinction in
the names and in the docs.

<a id="fr-10"></a>

## FR-10: Group helpers by family `[VIOLATED]`

> Each library owns one concern, and its name says which.

Old number: 2.6.

Check: impossible.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmCheats.sol:200-210` shows `_typeName`, which repeats the eight type names of `LibFheType.toString` (`host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/LibFheType.sol:42-52`) and differs only in the fallback. Fix: call `LibFheType.toString` and keep only the numeric fallback in the SDK.

Issues: I-16.

One concern, one library, and the name says which concern:
`LibFhevmHandle` owns the internal handle format (chain id, index, type byte, version), `LibFheType`
owns the type enum and its widths, `LibKmsVerifier` owns EIP-712 digests and decryption payloads,
`LibInputVerifier` owns input proofs. A helper that fits an existing family goes there, even when it
is one line; a helper that fits none is a sign a family is missing, not a reason to put it anywhere.
The same rule split `LibFheType` out of two duplicate `FheType` declarations and merged
`CleartextHandle` into `LibFhevmHandle` — both had produced silent drift first.

<a id="fr-11"></a>

## FR-11: Say what is not true `[HOLD]`

> A declaration says when its helper ignores an argument, cannot enforce something, or holds only under a condition.

Old number: 2.7.

Check: impossible.

If a helper ignores an argument, cannot enforce something, or holds
only under a condition, the declaration says so. Silent divergence is the failure mode this codebase
keeps hitting.

<a id="fr-12"></a>

## FR-12: A user never hears the word handle `[VIOLATED]`

> The public API speaks in encrypted types and clear values, never in `bytes32` handles.

Old number: 2.8.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Ten user-visible messages in `LibFhevmFail.sol` use the word handle. Lines not recorded. Fix: reword the messages.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-33: Are the 25 `bytes32` batch overloads of `decrypt` and `decryptPublic` the rule's "type cannot be known" exception?

Issues: I-12, I-33.

The public API speaks in encrypted types — `euint32`,
`ebool`, `eaddress` — and in clear values. A `bytes32` handle is how the stack stores a value, not how
a test talks about one: `plaintextOf(euint32)`, `forkUnknown(euint32, uint32)`, `decrypt(euint32, …)`.
An entry point that takes or returns a `bytes32` is a leak, and the fix is a typed overload, not a doc
comment — the only exception is a case where the type genuinely cannot be known at the call site, and
that case says so in its name. `unwrap` in a test is the symptom; a `seedCleartext(bytes32, uint256)`
with no typed overload is what this rule was written after.

<a id="fr-14"></a>

## FR-14: The SDK is user friendly, always `[VIOLATED]`

> Each public entry is one typed call in the vocabulary of the FHE library, with nothing for the user to wire.

Old number: 2.10.

Check: impossible.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmDecryptPublic.sol:138` shows `decryptPublic(bytes32 a, bytes32 b)`, a public entry that takes raw `bytes32` where the rule promises typed arguments. FR-12 counts the same defect. Fix: fix it with FR-12. The fix depends on D6.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-33: Are the 25 `bytes32` batch overloads of `decrypt` and `decryptPublic` the rule's "type cannot be known" exception?

Issues: I-16, I-33.

forge-fhevm-std is what a dApp developer types in a
test, not an internal of the mock stack. Every public entry is judged by the line a user writes: one
call, typed arguments, the vocabulary of the FHE library they already use (`euint32`, `encryptUint32`,
`decrypt`), nothing to wire and nothing to know about how the stack works underneath. The measure is
the fork test that reads as five lines — get, `forkUnknown`, encrypt, call, `decryptPublic` — where the
same work once took an `eventProcessor()`, an `unwrap`, a manual replay and three hardcoded addresses.
When a step is needed for the protocol, the SDK does it (the upgrade to cleartext, the signer swap, the
address resolution); when a step is needed from the user, one call with a plain name does it. A helper that is
correct but awkward is not done — [FR-12](../entries/FR-12.md) and [FR-13](../entries/FR-13.md) are this rule applied twice.

<a id="fr-15"></a>

## FR-15: A setup failure tells the user how to fix it `[VIOLATED]`

> A setup failure reverts with a loud message that says what happened, why, and the line that fixes it.

Old number: 2.11.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/LibFhevmFail.sol:65` shows the FORK DRIFT message, which tells the user that the FHE events were not drained. Nothing drains since the replay was removed (`foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:599-603`). Fix: correct the FORK DRIFT text.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmChains.sol:149,153,160,177,183,251,256` show that a wrong chain alias reverts with a plain `require` string, not through `LibFhevmFail`. Fix: render the chain-table failures through `LibFhevmFail`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/LibFhevmFail.sol:342-349` shows the NO PLAINTEXT SOURCE message, which names a replay and can no longer fire, because `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/FhevmVm.sol:1265` always sets the plaintext source. Fix: delete `noPlaintextsSource`.

Issues: I-34.

Everything that can go wrong because a
test is SET UP wrong — the `fhevm` handle missing, a fork entered through `vm` instead of `fhevm` (drift),
a fork whose stack was never named, a chain running a protocol version this SDK does not vendor, a
deployer nonce that is not where the local deploy expects it, a cheat called on the wrong kind of stack —
reverts with an ASCII-decorated, multi-line message that says WHAT happened, WHY it is refused, and the
exact line that FIXES it. Never a bare `EvmError: Revert`, never "call to non-contract address", never a
custom error whose selector the user has to decode. The measure: a developer who has never read this
package's source pastes the message and knows what to type next. Detect at the point closest to the
cause — `setUp`, a constructor, the first SDK entry — not where the consequence surfaces. All such
messages go through one helper so they look alike; tests match them with the same helper, so a reworded
message is a one-line change. (Errors that are NOT setup issues — a permit the ACL refuses, a handle the
replay never saw — stay typed custom errors: they are what a test asserts on.)

<a id="fr-29"></a>

## FR-29: `Forge` in a name means it touches cheatcodes `[CONFLICT]`

> A name contains `Forge` only when its code uses cheatcodes.

Old number: 5.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-05.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-29: Does "carries `Forge` in its name" apply to every file in `pkg/src` that uses the VM, or only to host source and `_host/`?

Issues: I-13, I-29.

A reader must be able to tell from the file
list alone which code can never run on chain.

#### Name a file

For names, follow forge-std first. Where forge-std says nothing, follow this table:

| Kind                          | Pattern                                                             | Example                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| library                       | `Lib<Name>.sol`                                                     | `LibKmsVerifier`, `LibFheType`                      |
| library that uses cheatcodes  | `LibForgeFhevm<Name>.sol`                                           | `LibForgeFhevmEncrypt`, `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions` |
| contract that uses cheatcodes | `ForgeFhevm<Name>.sol`                                              | `ForgeFhevmDeploy`                                  |
| public API mixin              | `StdFhevm<Name>.sol`                                                | `StdFhevmEncrypt`, `StdFhevmDecrypt`                |
| cheats mixin                  | `…CheatsSafe`, with `…Cheats is …CheatsSafe` once a footgun appears | forge-std's `StdCheatsSafe`                         |
| interface                     | `I<Name>.sol`                                                       | `IForgeVm`, `IPlaintexts`                           |
| argument bundle               | `<Function>ArgsV1`                                                  | `UserDecryptPayloadArgsV1`                          |
| pinned to an ABI shape        | `V1`, last                                                          | `userDecryptV1OnForkStack`                          |

`Forge` in a name means cheatcodes, and nothing else. `LibHostUpgradeCode` patches bytecode and is pure, so its name has no `Forge`. `Host` in place of `Fhevm` means the host contracts rather than the SDK. That is why the version tables are `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions`: they use cheatcodes, and they are about the hosts.

<a id="fr-30"></a>

## FR-30: Name what a function returns `[HOLD]`

> A function name says what it returns, not how it got the result.

Old number: 5.2.

Check: impossible.

For example, the function that returns the plaintext of a handle is `plaintextOf`, not `read`. `read`
says how the function gets the value, and not what the value is.

Take the words from the vocabulary already in the stack: `plaintexts`, `handle`, `cleartext`, `permit`.

<a id="fr-31"></a>

## FR-31: A handle is always a `bytes32` `[HOLD]`

> A handle is always a `bytes32`, and a parameter of an encrypted type is a `value`.

Old number: 5.3.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14.

A parameter of an encrypted type is a `value`.

## FR-32: Match forge-std `[VIOLATED]`

> The public API follows the conventions of forge-std.

Old number: 6.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmDecrypt.sol:54,573,575`, `StdFhevmEncrypt.sol:257` and `StdFhevmDecryptPublic.sol:261` check arguments with `require` strings, not custom errors. These checks are not setup failures, so the exception of FR-15 does not cover them. Fix: convert the checks to custom errors. The fix depends on D7.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-34: Does "custom errors over `require` strings" cover argument checks in the public mixins?

Issues: I-34.

`internal` members on abstract contracts, inherited through `TestFhevm`;
overloads rather than `…Uint8`/`…Uint16` suffix soup where the type can carry it; custom errors over
`require` strings; cheats grouped in a `…Cheats` mixin.

<a id="fr-33"></a>

## FR-33: The public API takes no addresses `[CONFLICT]`

> A test names a stack once, and no `StdFhevm*` helper takes an address.

Old number: 6.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-16.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-39: Is `setProtocol` a user path, or internal?

Issues: I-13, I-39.

A test names a stack once — the constructor's local stack by default, `fhevm.createSelectFork(chain, …)` on a fork, or
`fhevm.setProtocol(...)` for a manual declaration — and every helper resolves from there. Address-taking
overloads belong to the libraries, not to `StdFhevm*`.

<a id="fr-34"></a>

## FR-34: Pausing is invisible to the caller `[CONFLICT]`

> Every public entry is `unmetered`, so a test measures only the gas of its dApp call.

Old number: 6.3.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-07.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-37: Does the gas-metering rule bind the cleartext mock contracts and the `view` helpers?

Issues: I-13, I-36, I-37.

Every public entry is `unmetered`, so a test's gas
figure measures only its dApp's call. That makes those entries non-`view`; do not add `view` back.
